URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/29/fighting-in-ethiopia-intensifies-whats-the-latest
Al Jazeera (Al Jazeera Staff) — published 29 September 2026

Government forces and their allies in Ethiopia say they have taken control of a strategic town in Tigray after days of fighting with rebel forces across multiple fronts.
The Tigray Peace Force, an armed group of Tigrayan fighters aligned with the federal government, said on Facebook that they had captured Alamata with the national army. Video verified by Reuters showed soldiers walking through Alamata carrying Ethiopian flags.
Alamata is about 120km (75 miles) south of Tigray's capital, Mekelle; it sits near Tigray's southern border with Amhara and serves as a supply hub for troops, fuel and food. Its capture could allow federal forces to push north towards Mekelle.
A military source told Al Jazeera that government forces had already advanced and were heading towards or surrounding the Tigrayan capital.
Fighting erupted last week when Tigrayan forces launched a major offensive, seizing three airports in Tigray (Mekelle, Axum, Shire) and pushing into the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions. The TPLF says it is fighting a "defensive war", accusing federal forces of attacks using drones and heavy artillery.
This is the most serious confrontation since the AU-brokered Pretoria Agreement of November 2022. The TPLF dominated Ethiopian politics for nearly three decades before Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed came to power in 2018.
Days before the latest offensive, the TPLF joined six other armed groups to form the Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Alliance for Survival, which says it wants to remove Abiy's government and establish a transitional administration.
Ethiopia's army chief, Field Marshal Berhanu Jula, has accused Eritrea of supporting the opposition and alleged that Sudan and Egypt are also providing backing.
Related (approved): https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c6d94wywx0ypo (BBC, 2026-09-25T23:42:39Z) — "Are Ethiopians marching back to war in Tigray?" The AU has called for an immediate cessation of hostilities and a return to direct talks, and has asked former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, the AU's special Horn of Africa envoy, to engage the parties urgently. The regional body Igad has also called for fighting to stop. The AU has urged all neighbouring countries not to take actions that could escalate the crisis.
